study type: Animal study (randomized controlled trial in piglets)
outcome: Density of F18 in intestinal mucosa
Acetic and butyric acids in colon contents
cohort: The participants were newborn caesarean-delivered, colostrum-deprived term piglets on parenteral nutrition for the first 15 hours, serving as models for sensitive newborn infants.
finding: The lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains (Lactobacillus paracasei F19 and Pediococcus pentosaceus) used in this study failed to reduce E. coli-induced diarrhoea in sensitive newborn pigs and in fact, LAB supplementation further increased the diarrhoea score relative to F18 alone.
